name: remove_cables
description: Remove cable pieces as wire cutters would: reference_ids, or the cable in each cell of waypoints or cells (positions in metres). A burnt cable (a CableRuptured piece such as StructureCableStraightBurnt, left by an overload: on no network, built by no coil) is removed too, by id or by its cell, and refunds nothing. Refused for a piece with a fuse or analyser mounted (the game refuses too), indestructible pieces or pieces of a launching or landing rocket (a rocket's pieces are removed as a player removes them, 1.6.0+). Guards and report as place_cables: would_split when a network would fall apart or a device port would be left joined to nothing, listing each part (networks_after) with its devices; allowed with allow_split. A network that only loses pieces keeps its id (pieces leave it before they are destroyed); a split is rebuilt by the game from the removed pieces' neighbours, with new ids. Refund (default true): what deconstructing gives back (refund false moves no item; only refund_to "source" needs a player or from_id), where refund_to says (default ["inventory", "source", "storage", "ground"], each tried in turn per item: the player's inventory, then topping up from_id when it is a stack, then from_id's slots and those of the container it is stored in, then the ground in front of the holder; a container's reference id is exactly that container; refund_to "source" keeps the old way: into from_id's inventory, default the player, and the player carrying it); each target tops up matching stacks first, then makes new stacks in empty slots that take the item, a holder's own slots before those of the items in them, never a hidden slot, a body slot or a stack's own slot (a cable coil's, whose contents the game destroys with it); the dry run's materials.refund_plan shows each item's destinations; only what nothing takes goes on the ground a metre in front of the outermost holder, at rest (never inside the player); with refund_to "source" a from_id stack stored in a holder (a coil in a locker) takes the refund onto itself only, and what does not fit on it goes on the ground in front of that holder (the default's storage target does use the holder's other slots); refunded lists each part with where: merged, slot or ground and the target it went to. Dry run by default; dry_run false and confirm true runs a tick-held job, polled with job_id. Host only. No gateway is needed. would_split (1.3.0+; ports left joined to nothing give one entry per network they were on, with its network_id) lists per resulting network its devices, the root (root, else every supplier on it) and cut_off, the devices no root reaches after the removal; root names the root device. Job slot (1.3.0+): while another job runs, a real run answers status busy with running_job_id (nothing changed); wait: true queues it instead (status queued, its own job_id, position; up to 8 wait), and it starts once the slot is free, its whole preflight run again on the world the earlier jobs left. Network handles (1.3.0+): wherever a network id is taken (network_id, to.network_id, join_to, allow_bridge entries) a reference id of any piece or device on the network, or {reference_id, port} of a device port, works too and is resolved to the current id when the call runs (ids change after almost every edit); the reply lists each in resolved_networks [{argument, given, network_id}]. In allow_bridge a bare device id stays the device (its ports may share a network); name one of its networks with {reference_id, port}. 1.14.0+: a chute network's riding items (networks_before items) are listed only with include_network_devices too (items_riding counts them); a brief job poll's log counts the placed pieces (placed_count) instead of naming each (created_ids holds every id built; verbose names them).

reference_ids.description: cable pieces to remove. Give one of reference_ids, waypoints or cells.

items.description: [x, y, z] or {x, y, z} in metres.

waypoints.description: Remove the cable in every cell along these straight lines.

items.description: [x, y, z] or {x, y, z} in metres.

cells.description: Remove the cable in each cell.

allow_split.description: Let the removal split networks or leave ports joined to nothing. Default false.

limit.description: Cells listed, default 5 (200 before 1.14.0); 0 lists none.
